orientation.batter_faces: Northeast. Home plate sits in the southwest of the site and the batter looks out toward center field to the northeast; left field is to the northwest (Edgar Martinez Drive S / Left Field Gate side) and right field to the southeast.
orientation.confidence: CONFIRMED (two independent shade/orientation sources agree the field faces northeast; corroborated by gate geography - Left Field Gate on Edgar Martinez Dr S, Home Plate Gate on the 1st Ave S side)
orientation.caveat: theshadium.com states 'T-Mobile Park has a 45 degree orientation (northeast-facing), which means center field points toward the northeast' but then contradicts itself by saying the batter faces southwest. The batter faces center field by definition, so batter_faces = NORTHEAST. wherestheshade.com independently states 'the baseball field facing northeast'. Practical consequence: the sun sets off toward the third-base/left-field (northwest) side, so the third-base side and behind-home-plate seats shade first and right-field/upper-deck-right seats bake longest.

numbering_direction.summary: Section numbers INCREASE counterclockwise as seen from above, i.e. from RIGHT FIELD, up the first-base line, past HOME PLATE, down the third-base line, out to LEFT FIELD. Low numbers = right field / first base side; high numbers = left field / third base side. Home plate is at the MIDDLE of each level's range (approx. 127-132 on Main, 224-236 on Club, 328-332 on View), NOT at the start. The outfield bleacher block (180-195) restarts its own sequence and also increases counterclockwise, running from the left-field corner (180) toward center field (195).

accessibility.summary: CONFIRMED from the official Mariners Access Guide for Guests with Disabilities. 'Accessible and companion seating are available at a wide range of price levels' and are distributed proportionately across every price tier and level rather than being concentrated in one zone; the club will seat an entire party together in adjacent wheelchair locations where possible. 'All T-Mobile Park entrances are accessible.' Primary accessible entries: Home Plate Gate, Left Field Gate, and the Center Field Gates on S Royal Brougham Way. Accessible parking is available day-of-game in the Mariners Garage (7-foot height limit) with a state-issued disabled plate/permit. ADA drop-off on S Royal Brougham Way in front of the Center Field Gates, at the Left Field Gates, and near the garage on Occidental Ave S between Edgar Martinez Drive and S Massachusetts St. Service animals are welcome throughout with escorted relief areas outside the park.
landmarks: Elevators servicing ALL levels: Home Plate Gate, Left Field Gate, and near Section 105
Elevator servicing Street, Main and Center Field Bleachers only: near Section 191
Escalators: Home Plate Gate, Left Field Gate, Section 143, Section 125

discovery.row_seat_conventions: ROWS ARE NUMBERS at T-Mobile Park, on every level - no lettered rows found in the baseball configuration. Examples verified on RateYourSeats section pages: 'Rows in Section 108 are labeled 23-41', 'Rows in Section 122 are labeled 5-41', 'Rows in Section 128 are labeled 17-43', 'Rows in Section 134 are labeled 9-41', 'Rows in Section 140 are labeled 1-41', 'Rows in Section 149 are labeled 12-41', 'Rows in Section 184 are labeled 1-12', 'Rows in Section 191 are labeled 1-17', 'Rows in Diamond Club 35 are labeled 1-8'. Row 1 is closest to the field. Row numbering does NOT always start at 1 - infield sections behind the Diamond Club and the dugouts start at Row 5, 9, 12, 17, 23 etc. because the premium seating in front consumes the low row numbers, so a Main Level section's row range is a reliable proxy for how far back the section sits. Typical row ceilings: Main Level up to Row 41-43; Club/Terrace Level roughly Rows 1-12; View Level 25 rows (1-29 at the widest), with the entry tunnel at Row 5. Seat counts per row vary (commonly 12-24) and some rows are inset (e.g. Section 184 Rows 4-8 have 19 seats labeled 3-21, i.e. seats 1-2 and 22-24 do not exist in those rows). Concert Field sections use LETTERS for the section (A-S, skipping I, O and Q) but numbers for rows. The only lettered-row claim found anywhere was MapaPlan's 'Row C, Section 35', which contradicts RateYourSeats' 'Rows in Diamond Club 35 are labeled 1-8' - treat that as a reseller artifact, UNCERTAIN.
discovery.seat1_side_verbatim: "When looking towards the field/stage, lower number seats are on the right" - quoted verbatim from RateYourSeats T-Mobile Park section pages (confirmed identical wording on Sections 108, 122, 128, 134, 140, 184 and 191). In plain terms: facing the field, SEAT 1 IS ON THE RIGHT and seat numbers increase toward your LEFT. Note this is the OPPOSITE of the common 'seat 1 on the left' convention, and it is also opposite in feel to the section numbering, which increases counterclockwise (right field toward left field). Source: https://www.rateyourseats.com/t-mobile-park/seating/sections/122
discovery.known_obstructions: 1) PROTECTIVE NETTING (official): 'Sections 115-146 will now be behind netting. The height and coverage vary by section. Netting in front of those seated in Sections 126-134 is 27-feet high. For those seated in Sections 115-125 and Sections 135-146, the netting will extend 13.5-feet above field level.' (https://www.mlb.com/mariners/ballpark/seat-map) 2) LIMITED/OBSTRUCTED VIEW sections flagged by ticketing inventory: 110, 111, 149, 150 (Main Level outfield corners), 211, 212, 248, 249 (Club Level ends), 314, 346, 347, 349 (View Level ends) - source https://www.mapaplan.com/seating-plan/seattle-tmobile-park-stadium-detailed-interactive-seat-row-numbers-chart-plan/seattle-tmobile-park-stadium-seating-chart-plan.htm 3) Deep corner and down-the-line Main Level sections (102-110 in right field, 146-151 in left field) have sharp viewing angles into the near corner of the outfield. 4) Roof support trusses and the upper-deck overhang cast structural shadows and can clip sightlines to the scoreboard from the back rows of the Main Level and from Club rows under the View Level overhang. 5) Rear rows of the Main Level infield (Rows ~35+) sit under the Club Level overhang - good for shade and rain, but the very top of fly balls and the video board can be cut off.
discovery.roof_and_dry_seats: The retractable roof COVERS but DOES NOT ENCLOSE the ballpark. Wikipedia: the roof 'does not fully enclose the ballpark; this allows the wind and temperatures to still impact the game with the roof closed.' It spans roughly nine acres, weighs 22 million pounds, and takes 10-20 minutes to open or close, parking on rails east of the stadium. Ballparks of Baseball: 'The retractable roof covers the entire stadium without fully enclosing it, preserving an open-air atmosphere.' STAY DRY: the infield bowl and the upper rows of the Main Level infield (roughly sections 116-144, Rows 35+, under the Club overhang), the Club/Terrace Level (Rows 10 and above), and the View Level sections well back under the upper roof - RateYourSeats notes 'Sections 333-344 are among the first to get shade and are well covered from the upper deck roof' and that View Level outfield sections are 'well protected by the retractable roof, even when open'. GET WET ANYWAY: 'Even with the roof closed, seats in the outfield and upper deck are susceptible to blowing rain' because the sides of the park remain open - this applies especially to the outfield bleachers 180-195, the low rows of the Main Level, and the exposed ends of the View Level. Source: https://www.rateyourseats.com/t-mobile-park/seating/shaded-covered-seats ; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/T-Mobile_Park ; https://www.ballparksofbaseball.com/ballparks/t-mobile-park/
